日本語

Arare Reference

Arare quantizes by design and accounts for the precision it gives up. A number has a width (8, 16, 32 or 64 bits) and a scale exponent e: its value is its code times 2^e. Arithmetic widens to a width that holds the exact result; rounding happens only at QUANTIZE, RESCALE and DIV.

For every value a program leaves, the error-budget checker infers, without running it, how far Arare's value may be from the exact value Ajisai computes. A program is field=closed when the checker bounds every numeric result; otherwise it is field=open, and the checker says which Word and why.

Each sample opens in the Playground, which runs it in Arare and in Ajisai side by side and shows the difference against the budget.

  • Numbers and rounding QUANTIZE RESCALE NARROW
  • Arithmetic ADD SUB MUL DIV NEG
  • Comparison EQ LT
  • Truth AND NOT SELECT
  • Blocks and aggregates FILTER MAP FOLD SUM
  • Literals TRUE FALSE NIL
  • Names BIND

Words

QUANTIZE

Puts x at a width and scale exponent; how a non-integer enters a program.

Syntax: x width exponent QUANTIZE (AR-HLR-018, AR-HLR-026)

Width
The width named: 8, 16, 32 or 64.
Scale
The exponent named, within ±31.
Error
Raising the exponent rounds half to even, adding at most half an ulp of the new scale; lowering it is exact. A literal p/q is rounded once, where it is written.
field
Open (mayOverflow) when the value may not fit the width: it is then 1/0. Writing 1/0 or 0/0 is open (wheelPoint).
Samples
SourceResultBudget
1/3 8 -6 QUANTIZE 21/64 ± 1/192 Open in Playground
2.75 8 -1 QUANTIZE 3/1 ± 1/4 Open in Playground
1 8 -7 QUANTIZE 1/0 none Open in Playground

ADD

The exact sum, lane by lane.

Syntax: a b ADD (AR-HLR-003, AR-HLR-005, AR-HLR-022)

Width
Widened to the narrowest width that holds the sum of the operands' ranges; int64 at most.
Scale
The smaller of the two exponents: the other operand is shifted to it exactly.
Error
Exact: the result's budget is the sum of the operands' budgets.
field
Open when the sum may leave int64 (mayOverflow) or an operand is a wheel point.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
126 1 ADD 127/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground
0.5 8 -1 QUANTIZE 3 ADD 7/2 ± 0/1 Open in Playground
[ 1 2 3 ] [ 10 ] ADD [ 11/1 12/1 13/1 ] ± 0/1 Open in Playground

SUB

The exact difference a − b, lane by lane.

Syntax: a b SUB (AR-HLR-003, AR-HLR-005, AR-HLR-022)

Width
As ADD: the narrowest width holding the difference of the ranges.
Scale
The smaller of the two exponents.
Error
Exact: the budgets add.
field
As ADD.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
7 3 SUB 4/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground
[ 5 6 ] [ 1 2 ] SUB [ 4/1 4/1 ] ± 0/1 Open in Playground

MUL

The exact product, lane by lane.

Syntax: a b MUL (AR-HLR-003, AR-HLR-006, AR-HLR-022)

Width
Widened to the narrowest width holding the product of the ranges: int8 × int8 is int16.
Scale
The sum of the two exponents; an exponent beyond ±31 is an ERROR.
Error
Exact: each operand's budget is scaled by the other's range, as the product propagates it.
field
Open when the product may leave int64 or an operand is a wheel point.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
100 100 MUL 10000/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground
[ 1 2 3 ] [ 4 5 6 ] MUL [ 4/1 10/1 18/1 ] ± 0/1 Open in Playground
1/3 8 -6 QUANTIZE [ 1 2 ] MUL [ 21/64 21/32 ] ± 1/96 Open in Playground

DIV

The quotient a / b, rounded: one of Arare's three rounding points.

Syntax: a b DIV (AR-HLR-007, AR-HLR-022)

Width
The narrowest width holding the dividend's range shifted by the divisor's exponent.
Scale
The dividend's exponent: write the dividend at a finer scale for a finer quotient.
Error
Rounds half to even: adds at most half an ulp of the result's scale.
field
Open (divisorMayBeZero) when the divisor may be 0: x/0 is 1/0 and 0/0 is ⊥.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
7 2 DIV 4/1 ± 1/2 Open in Playground
1 8 -6 QUANTIZE 3 DIV 21/64 ± 1/128 Open in Playground
1 0 DIV 0 0 DIV 1/0 0/0 ± 0/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground

NEG

The negation; 1/0 and 0/0 are their own.

Syntax: a NEG (AR-HLR-002, AR-HLR-003, AR-HLR-022)

Width
Unchanged: finite ranges are symmetric.
Scale
Unchanged.
Error
Exact: the budget is the operand's.
field
Open only when the operand is a wheel point.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
1 2 SUB NEG 1/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground

RESCALE

Raises x's exponent by s bits (0 to 62), rounding: one of the three rounding points.

Syntax: x s RESCALE (AR-HLR-008, AR-HLR-022)

Width
Unchanged.
Scale
Raised by s.
Error
Rounds half to even: adds at most half an ulp of the new scale; a value already on the grid is unchanged.
field
No effect of its own; a wheel point passes through.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
1000 2 RESCALE 1000/1 ± 2/1 Open in Playground
0.75 8 -2 QUANTIZE 1 RESCALE 1/1 ± 1/4 Open in Playground

NARROW

Fits x into a narrower width; a value that does not fit is 1/0, never clamped.

Syntax: x width NARROW (AR-HLR-009, AR-HLR-022)

Width
The width named.
Scale
Unchanged.
Error
Exact when the value fits.
field
Open (mayOverflow) when the value may not fit the width.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
100 100 MUL 100 SUB 16 NARROW 9900/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground
300 8 NARROW 1/0 none Open in Playground

EQ

Whether two values denote the same, whatever their widths and scales; always TRUE or FALSE.

Syntax: a b EQ (AR-HLR-010, AR-HLR-022)

Width
A truth value, not a number.
Scale
Operands are aligned exactly before they are compared.
Error
The checker says whether Arare's answer agrees with Ajisai's: it does when the values are exact or their ranges, widened by their budgets, are apart.
field
No effect of its own.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
2 0.5 8 -1 QUANTIZE 4 MUL EQ TRUE ± 0/1 Open in Playground
[ 1 2 ] [ 2 1 ] EQ FALSE ± 0/1 Open in Playground

LT

Whether a < b, lane by lane; asked of a wheel point, UNKNOWN.

Syntax: a b LT (AR-HLR-011, AR-HLR-022)

Width
A truth value, not a number.
Scale
Operands are aligned exactly before they are compared.
Error
Agrees with Ajisai when both values are exact or their ranges, widened by their budgets, are apart.
field
No effect of its own.
Samples
SourceResultBudget
1 2 LT 2 1 LT TRUE FALSE ± 0/1 ± 0/1 Open in Playground
1 0 DIV 1 LT NIL ± 0/1 Open in Playground

AND

Strong Kleene conjunction: FALSE settles it, NIL reads as UNKNOWN.

Syntax: a b AND (AR-HLR-012, AR-HLR-013, AR-HLR-022)

Width
Truth values only.
Scale
—
Error
Agrees with Ajisai when its operands do.
field
No effect.

Syntax: a NOT (AR-HLR-012, AR-HLR-013, AR-HLR-022)

Truth values only.

—

FILTER

Keeps the elements the block calls TRUE; FALSE, UNKNOWN and NIL drop them, as SQL's WHERE does.

Syntax: vector [ predicate ] FILTER (AR-HLR-014, AR-HLR-024)

Width
The elements keep theirs.
Scale
The elements keep theirs.
Error
The elements keep their budgets.
field
Whatever the block does.

FOLD

Threads an accumulator through the block, element by element from the left.

Syntax: vector initial [ block ] FOLD (AR-HLR-024)

Width
What the block gives the accumulator.
Scale
What the block gives the accumulator.
Error
Accumulated step by step; the checker coarsens long loops so a budget stays computable.
field
Whatever the block does at any step.
Samples
SourceResultBudget

SUM

The sum of a vector's elements, skipping NIL as SQL does; all NIL is NIL.

Syntax: vector SUM (AR-HLR-016)

Width
Widened to hold the sum of every lane.
Scale
The elements' exponent.
Error
Exact: the lanes' budgets add.
field
Open when the sum may leave int64.

SELECT

THEN where the condition is TRUE, ELSE otherwise: UNKNOWN takes ELSE, as SQL's CASE does.

Syntax: then else condition SELECT (AR-HLR-015, AR-HLR-022)

Width
Wide enough for either side.
Scale
Either side's.
Error
Either side's budget, when the condition agrees with Ajisai's.
field
No effect of its own.
